messages:
lee: quick poll: for the inference-config APIshould we serve proto/gRPC internally and have gateway transcode to JSON for external clients, or flatten to REST at the gateway and keep backends JSON?

anika: my leaning: gRPC+proto inside. typed contracts help us avoid subtle schema drift and reduce integration bugs.

pat: +1 for typed backend. but weneed to be explicit about where quota enforcement and routing decisions live. gateway or backend?

mike: If gateway enforces quotas, it has to see the auth token and tenant. But if backend re-checks we risk double-counting or inconsistent limits.

lee: UX concern: product teams consume Console docs. If we transcode at gateway then console should show canonical REST shapes. If backend is the source of truth we should surface generated client libs in Console.

anika: telemetry: gRPC gives access to per-message trailers and streaming metadata. transcode layers often drop trailers unless we copy them into headers. Need a mapping table.

pat: operational modes:
- shared gateway transcode (one place to maintain)
- per-pod sidecar adapter (local, lower latency)
- hybrid: transcode gateway + optional sidecar for hot paths

mike: sidecar pros: trace spans stay local, no extra hop for metadata. cons: more images to maintain and harder canarying.

lee: example gateway route prototype: 
```
- match: POST /v1/config/infer
  to: inference-config.svc.cluster.local:443
  protocol: grpc
  transcode: true
  pass_headers: [x-tenant, x-request-id, authorization]
  quota_scope: header:x-tenant
```

anika: important: define EXACT header names and semantics. x-tenant vs x-org vs tenant-id confusion caused a few nasty incidents last year.

pat: what about error semantics? gRPC has rich status codes and details. When we transcode, do we map them to HTTP codes + structured body? We should standardize that to avoid clients misparsing.

mike: yes, mapping table: gRPC NOT_FOUND -> 404, PERMISSION_DENIED -> 403, UNAUTHENTICATED -> 401, INTERNAL -> 502 with error_id. include original gRPC code in body for debugging.

lee: rollout plan suggestion:
1) implement gateway transcode with strict header propagation (canary)
2) instrument telemetry mapping and validate parity of traces/metrics
3) add console toggle to expose proto SDKs for teams that want typed clients
4) evaluate sidecars for latency-critical endpoints

anika: action items:
- I will draft header contract doc + integration tests (lee)
- pat: prototype gRPC->http error mapping and add test vectors
- mike: telemetry mapping spec (trailer->header) and sampling checks
- ops-bot: schedule canary after docs ready

ops-bot: deploy queued: gateway-transcode-prototype v0.2 -> canary 2025-10-12T14:00Z

pat: small question: who owns quota telemetry? gateway emits usage, backend should still log request for auditing but not decrement quota. who writes the console UI?

lee: Console team will add a per-route affordance: "quota_enforced_by: gateway|backend". Default to gateway for external routes; backend for internal-only.

anika: +1. Also add a migration checklist for services switching ownership.

mike: no blockers from infra side. will add a trace-correlator filter to copy trailers into headers for transcode lanes.

lee: thanks everyone. if no objections I'll open RFC PR with the plan and link the prototype.

anika: no objections. :thumbsup:

pat: +1

mike: +1

lee: RFC PR opened: https://phabricator.internal/r/CI-2042 (will post diff and tests)
